copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Qatar and Switzerland together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Qatar side, by +17.6pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Qatar 1720 vs Switzerland 1840: 120 points in favour of Switzerland, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Qatar to win at 26%, the draw at 23%, and Switzerland to win at 51%. The home side reads 26% on this distribution — the model's central case for Qatar.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Qatar to win at 8%, the draw at 16%, and Switzerland to win at 76%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Qatar side — 8% on the market, 26% on the engine, a +17.6pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Qatar the lower bound is 20%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +12.0pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Qatar side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 25 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +17.6pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +17.6pp gap across model and market on the Qatar side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Qatar at 26%; Polymarket sits at 8%.
copy.title: Qatar v Switzerland · the model leans Qatar
